content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom happens when you previously attached a file but now the previous containing folder no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed. When you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail, that is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug has been fixed for the next release, due next week.

In the meantime, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you're comfortable delving into Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

- In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".

- The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).

- The Attach button should work again right away - it's not necessary to restart Thunderbird.

content:
The easy way is to

  1. install the addon, importexporttools NG
  2. then, highlight Local Folders
  3. rightclick and select the importexport option to import mbox and then select that file.

This creates a folder in Local Folder, where you can review that all is well. With that much mail , it can be difficult to merger with the existing sent folder. My cautious approach would be to leave it in Local Folders.

I would also save that sent.mbox file separately as a backup. And, since POP and PCs and software do sometimes crash, I suggest periodic backups. Save these steps in case something crashes:


BACKUP

  1. ensure thunderbird is not running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. this should open windows file explorer in Appdata\roaming folder
  4. highlight the Thunderbird folder and copy to external media

RESTORE

  1. ensure thunderbird is installed, run once, and NOT running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. delete the thunderbird folder
  4. you should be in Appdata\roaming folder , copy&paste the exported Thunderbird folder there.
  5. start thunderbird and all should be there

I can see from examining a Thunderbird mbox folder file with a text editor (Notepad++) that each new message begins like this. It's plain ASCII text:

From - Thu Oct 08 16:39:34 2026 X-Mozilla-Status: 0001 X-Mozilla-Status2: 00000000

Sample date, of course, but this shows the format.

The X-Mozilla-Status codes are defined here:

https://vincent.bernat.ch/en/x-mozilla-status

I notice from looking at a many-years-old folder, that the messages were separated with only "From ". But after Repairing and Compacting it, it now has the date and X-Mozilla headers added, which suggests to me that the format was changed sometime in the past, presumably to make it less fragile.

content:
That "mailnews.tcptimeout" is probably overkill. The value represents how many seconds it will wait before giving up on trying to connect to the server. If it really takes over a half-hour to connect you've got bigger problems than that setting. It probably doesn't hurt anything, but I'd still dial it back to something more reasonable, like maybe 120 - 300.

The first thing to do is to confirm that you have the correct settings. Here are Spectrum's recommendations. Not that the exact ones depend on your provider's name/domain:

https://www.spectrum.net/support/internet/mobile-email-setup

Try restarting Thunderbird in Troubleshoot Mode (see <Help | Troubleshoot Mode>.) Among other things, this will disable all add-ons, in case one is misbehaving. I suspect this isn't your problem, though.

Computer anti-virus and Internet security programs are notorious for interfering with email connections. If you use any, try temporarily disabling it or creating an exception for Thunderbird.

Be aware that Spectrum has a history of intermittent connection issues. There was a spate of them a few months ago. Spectrum's front like tech support either didn't know about them or didn't understand them or just wouldn't admit it. If you could get through to the next level, they DID admit it, though they didn't offer a solution. Eventually they fixed the problem on their end and it went away. In other words, it was never a Thunderbird issue. That was not the first time. I don't know if this applies to you now, except to keep in mind that Spectrum email is not very reliable.
